speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash; to begin my assessment, how many days old is the baby and what does the rash look like? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Blood_Culture, Blood_Smear. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Newborn_Rash.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Varicella (Chickenpox). The clinical picture of a generalized erythematous maculopapular rash with pustules on an erythematous base, involving the trunk and extremities while sparing the palms and soles, is classic for varicella in a newborn. Given the urgency and the presence of pustules, immediate isolation and treatment with IV Acyclovir are indicated.
